p.src: A Newtonian point mass and a Schwarzschild black hole begin with the same idealization: all the gravitating mass is concentrated at the center. Their centers nevertheless have very different meanings. In Newtonian mechanics a particle with even a little angular momentum misses the center. In a black hole, once the particle has crossed the horizon, the singularity cannot be missed. Understanding that difference will take us through circular orbits, the photon sphere, and finally a new set of coordinates near the horizon.

ja: ニュートン的な点質量とシュヴァルツシルトブラックホールは、同じ理想化から出発する。すなわち、重力を及ぼす質量のすべてが中心に集中しているという理想化である。それにもかかわらず、両者の中心の意味は大きく異なる。ニュートン力学では、わずかでも角運動量をもつ粒子は中心を外れる。ブラックホールでは、粒子が事象の地平面を一度越えてしまえば、特異点を外れることはできない。この違いを理解するために、円軌道、光子球、そして最終的には地平面近傍の新しい座標系を順に見ていくことになる。
zh: 牛顿力学中的质点与史瓦西黑洞始于同一个理想化假设：所有产生引力的质量都集中在中心。然而，它们的中心却有着截然不同的含义。在牛顿力学中，即使只带有一点角动量的粒子也不会击中中心。而在黑洞中，一旦粒子越过视界，奇点就无法被避开。理解这一差异将带领我们依次考察圆轨道、光子球，最后是视界附近的一套新坐标。

p.src:
Far from the source, $2MG/r$ is small and Eq. [eq:l6-schwarzschild] approaches the Minkowski metric in spherical coordinates. Two radii stand out: $r=2MG,

r=0.$ They must not be confused. At $r=2MG$, the coefficient of $dt^{2}$ vanishes and that of $dr^{2}$ diverges. The Schwarzschild coordinate system has become singular. p.src:
There is also no explicit $t$ in $\mathcal L$. The Hamiltonian is therefore conserved: $\begin{aligned}E=H
&=p_r\dot r+L\dot\theta-\mathcal L \\
&=\frac{mG\dot r^{\,2}}{\sqrt{\Delta}}
  +\frac{mr^{2}\dot\theta^{\,2}}{\sqrt{\Delta}}
  +m\sqrt{\Delta} \\
&=\frac{mF}{\sqrt{\Delta}}.
\end{aligned}$ This is a characteristic rhythm of mechanics. A principle gives the action; a calculation gives the momenta; symmetry then turns the calculation back into the principles of energy and angular-momentum conservation. One could immediately solve all the Euler–Lagrange equations, but the constants supplied by rotational and time-translation symmetry eliminate much of that work.

p.src:
A photon has energy and momentum even though its rest mass vanishes. The massless limit of Eq. [eq:l6-circular-energy] must consequently be taken with care. If $m$ went to zero at fixed $\lambda$, then $L=m\lambda$ would also vanish. Instead take $m\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\lambda\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
L=m\lambda\ \text{fixed}.$ The $\lambda^{2}$ term then dominates, and the photon energy becomes $E_\gamma(r;L)
=L\,\frac{\sqrt{1-\frac{2MG}{r}}}{r}.$ The factor $L$ multiplies the entire radial function. It affects the energy scale but not the radius of a circular orbit.

Just outside the photon sphere, a ray can sweep through a very large angle, perhaps winding around the hole many times, before escaping. Just inside it, a nearly tangential ray can wind several times and then fall through the horizon.

ja: 受講者からの質問: なぜ角運動量を固定するのか、またそれは光子の振動数や入射軌道とどう関係するのか。

p.src: Response: Every ray carries a conserved angular momentum about the black hole. Its frequency fixes the magnitude of its linear momentum, while its offset from the center helps determine $L$. Away from a circular orbit, radius and angular momentum may be chosen independently. Requiring a circular photon orbit links the motion to the unique radius $3MG$, and the factorization in Eq. [eq:l6-photon-energy] shows that this radius is independent of the magnitude of $L$. p.src: The photon sphere explains why a black hole is not merely a dark disk pasted over an otherwise unchanged sky. Light from a background object can reach an observer along several paths. One ray may pass on one side of the hole, another on the other side, and still others may circle the hole one or more times. The result can contain displaced images, duplicated images, rings, and an infinite sequence of ever finer, ever fainter images associated with additional windings. The exact picture is complicated, but its origin is already contained in the unstable orbit.

ja: 光子球は、ブラックホールが、他の点では変わらない空に貼り付けられた単なる暗い円盤ではない理由を説明する。背景天体からの光は複数の経路に沿って観測者に到達しうる。ある光線は穴の一方の側を通り、別の光線は反対側を通り、さらに別の光線は穴のまわりを1回以上周りうる。その結果には、ずれた像、重複した像、環、および追加の巻き付きに対応する、ますます細かくますます暗い像の無限列が含まれうる。正確な像は複雑であるが、その起源はすでに不安定軌道に含まれている。
zh: 光子球解释了为什么黑洞不仅仅是一个贴在原本不变的天空上的暗盘。来自背景天体的光可以沿多条路径到达观测者。一条光线可以从黑洞的一侧经过，另一条从另一侧经过，还有别的光线可能绕黑洞一圈或更多圈。结果可能包含位移的像、重复的像、环，以及与额外绕行圈数相关的无限序列的越来越精细、越来越暗淡的像。确切的图像很复杂，但其起源已经包含在那条不稳定轨道之中。

p.src: When source, lens, and observer are sufficiently aligned, the image can form an Einstein ring. Gravitational-lensing rings are observed in nature. The full black-hole image requires integrating the null geodesics for many initial directions, a calculation well suited to a computer.

Begin with two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime: $d\tau^{2}=dT^{2}-dX^{2}.$ In the right Rindler wedge define $X=\rho\cosh\omega,
\qquad
T=\rho\sinh\omega.$ Curves of constant $\rho$ obey $X^{2}-T^{2}=\rho^{2},$ so they are hyperbolae, the worldlines of uniformly accelerated observers. Substituting Eq. [eq:l6-rindler-map] into the flat metric gives $d\tau^{2}
=\rho^{2}d\omega^{2}-d\rho^{2}.$ Now set $\rho^{2}=4\xi,
\qquad
\omega=\frac{t}{2}.$ Since $d\rho^{2}=d\xi^{2}/\xi$, Eq. [eq:l6-rindler-metric] becomes $d\tau^{2}
=\xi\,dt^{2}-\frac{d\xi^{2}}{\xi}.$

p.src: Crossing the Rindler Horizon

u.src: Crossing the Rindler Horizon
en: Crossing the Rindler Horizon
ja: Rindler 地平線の横断
zh: 穿越 Rindler 视界

p.src:
The right-wedge formulas cover only $\xi>0$: $X=2\sqrt{\xi}\cosh\frac{t}{2},
\qquad
T=2\sqrt{\xi}\sinh\frac{t}{2}.$ The surface $\xi=0$ is the null line $X=T$. To continue into the future wedge, let $\zeta=-\xi>0$ and interchange the hyperbolic roles: $T=2\sqrt{\zeta}\cosh\frac{t}{2},
\qquad
X=2\sqrt{\zeta}\sinh\frac{t}{2}.$ The metric is still $d\tau^{2}
=\xi\,dt^{2}-\frac{d\xi^{2}}{\xi},$ but when $\xi<0$, the coefficient of $dt^{2}$ is negative and the coefficient of $d\xi^{2}$ is positive. The coordinate $\xi$, and hence the Schwarzschild radial direction, has become time-like; $t$ has become space-like.

zh: 现在这条零线被认作视界本身，而不仅仅是一个坐标系数表现失常的点。在它外部，一族径向光线向外运动。在它内部，两个未来光锥方向都指向更小的$r$。每一条指向未来的有质量轨迹都必须保持在这些零方向之间，因此会到达奇点。

p.src: Suppose collapsing matter emits a regular sequence of light pulses. A distant observer receives the later pulses at increasingly long intervals. Their frequencies shift from optical toward infrared, microwave, radio, and still longer wavelengths. In an idealized classical calculation the outside observer can continue to associate ever later signals with matter approaching the horizon, but the source rapidly becomes too red and too faint to detect in practice.

ja: 崩壊する物質が規則的な光パルスの列を放出するとしよう。遠方の観測者は、後のパルスをますます長い間隔で受け取る。それらの振動数は、可視光から赤外線、マイクロ波、電波へと移り、さらに長い波長へとずれていく。理想化された古典的計算では、外側の観測者は、地平線に近づく物質にますます後の信号を対応づけ続けることができるが、実際には光源は急速に赤くなりすぎ、暗くなりすぎて検出できなくなる。

p.src: How, then, can a black hole form or increase its mass if the outside observer never sees matter cross? Consider a collapsing spherical shell. The external Schwarzschild description still makes the shell approach the final horizon asymptotically. The complete spacetime picture, including how the horizon is located globally, is the subject of the next lecture.

p.src: The horizon and photon sphere divide the ray problem into distinct cases. At a radius $2MG<r<3MG,$ a radially outgoing light ray can escape to infinity. After the horizon is crossed, it closes completely.

p.src: The last question is intentionally less settled. Imagine Alice and Bob both held at the same radius outside the horizon. Nearby observers can plainly exchange signals. If they are far apart around the sphere, the direct null path and its limiting angular range require an explicit geodesic calculation. The class proposes an indirect route: send the message nearly radially outward to a relay at a safer radius, carry it around there, and send it back inward. Another version lets an outward-thrown object or signal turn around and return. These routes show why failure of a tangential circular orbit does not by itself forbid all communication between exterior observers.

ja: 最後の問いは意図的に未解決の度合いが高い。アリスとボブがともに地平面の外側の同じ半径に保持されていると想像しよう。近くの観測者どうしは明らかに信号を交換できる。彼らが球の周りで遠く離れている場合、直接のヌル経路とその限界角範囲を求めるには明示的な測地線計算が必要である。クラスは間接的な経路を提案する。すなわち、メッセージをほぼ動径方向に外側へ、より安全な半径にある中継点へ送り、そこで周囲を運び、再び内側へ送り返すのである。別の版では、外向きに投げられた物体または信号が向きを変えて戻ることを許す。これらの経路は、接線方向の円軌道が存在しないからといって、それだけで外部観測者間のあらゆる通信が禁じられるわけではない理由を示している。
zh: 最后一个问题有意地不那么确定。设想Alice和Bob都被保持在视界之外的同一半径处。附近的观测者显然可以交换信号。如果他们围绕球面相距很远，那么直接的零路径及其极限角范围需要显式的测地线计算。课堂提出了一条间接路线：将信息几乎径向向外发送到更安全半径处的中继站，在那里携带它绕行，然后再向内发送回来。另一种版本让向外抛出的物体或信号掉头返回。这些路线说明了为什么切向圆轨道的失败本身并不禁止外部观测者之间的一切通信。

p.src: Response: Locally, yes. For widely separated or diametrically opposite observers, the direct-path limit was not worked out in the lecture and should not be promoted to a theorem. The discussion first leaves that angular-geodesic question open, then observes that an indirect signal can go nearly radially outward, be relayed around at larger radius, and return. Approaching the horizon makes the directly useful angular range increasingly narrow, but outside the horizon an outward route remains available.  (Lecture timestamp: 02:01:29–02:04:17)

ja: 回答: 局所的には、できる。広く離れた、または正反対側にある観測者については、直接経路の限界は講義では導出されておらず、定理に格上げすべきではない。議論はまずその角方向測地線の問題を未解決のままにし、次に間接的な信号がほぼ動径方向に外側へ進み、より大きな半径で周囲を中継され、戻ってくることができると述べる。地平面に近づくにつれて直接役立つ角範囲はますます狭くなるが、地平面の外側では外向きの経路が依然として利用可能である。  (講義時刻: 02:01:29–02:04:17)
zh: 回答: 局部地，能。对于相距很远或正好相对的观测者，直接路径的极限在讲座中并未算出，不应被提升为定理。讨论首先将那个角向测地线问题留作未决，然后指出间接信号可以几乎径向向外发送，在较大半径处被中继绕行，然后返回。接近视界会使直接有用的角范围越来越窄，但在视界之外，向外路线仍然可用。  (讲课时间: 02:01:29–02:04:17)
